title: Personnel of the new Basie big band
summary: He recalls Jaws, Frank Foster, Frank Wess, Charlie Fowlkes, Marshall Royal, the Wilkins brothers and bassist Eddie Jones.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, so, okay, so he decided to get a big band.
He decided to form his big band again. And that's when the personnel was changed again.
Well, that's when he got Jaws in the band, I guess.
Well, yes, Jaws was in the band, and --
Neither of the Franks were in the band, Foster or Wes.
Let's see, they were in the band, but
not when we first started. He picked up Frank and West later. I think Frank Foster was in there first, then Frank West, and he had Charlie Fowlkes.
Yeah. He didn't have Bobby Pater.
Oh, no, no, none of those.
That was much later. And he didn't have Marshall.
Marshall Royal? He came in later also. We had two brothers in there. One played trombone and one played alto. And he did a lot of the arranging. Hey, Nell.
What, honey?
Who was the alto player that played with Basie, the real skinny --
Coker? Coker?
No, Coker played trombone. And he had a brother played trombone also. We saw him not too very long ago. He turned out to be a junkie, once.
Well, I don't know, I don't know. No, all right, we'll think of it.
(Recording interrupted.)
That was Ernie Wilkins, and his brother, Jimmy Wilkins. He played the trombone.
Yeah, yeah. And who did you have playing bass?
We had three or four bass players at
one time. Oh, Eddie Jones. Eddie Jones was playing bass.
Yeah, so he had a nice rhythm section.
Oh, yeah, a good rhythm section, a very good rhythm section.
